paper_title: Constraints on dark photon dark matter using data from LIGO's and Virgo's third observing run
notes: LIGO/Virgo O3 search for dark-photon dark matter coupled to baryon number U(1)_B. Headline curve is the BSD-method 95% CL upper limit (black line in Fig. 3, file O3_DPDM_UL_erratum.png = the updated erratum version), which the caption states is the most constraining at most masses; the red cross-correlation curve is weaker after the erratum correction. y-axis is eps^2_95%, where eps is the dark-photon/baryon coupling normalized to the EM coupling e (L = -eps*e*J^mu A_mu, J^mu = baryon-number current); I report chi = sqrt(eps^2), treating the paper's normalized coupling eps as the dark-photon coupling (paper-native value, no e-factor applied). Mass from m_A = h*f (m_A[eV]=4.1357e-15*f[Hz]); frequency range 10-2000 Hz -> m_A ~ 4.3e-14 to 8.3e-12 eV. Pixel-traced the black BSD continuum (lower/best-limit envelope, excluding the upward noise-line spikes) from the raster PNG, calibrated on the log axes (x: 10/100/1000 Hz major ticks; y: 1e-40..1e-48), and scaled by 1.30 so the minimum matches the paper's quoted best BSD value eps^2 = 2.4e-47 at m_A ~ 5.7e-13 eV. dm_density_assumed = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 (paper: rho_DM = 4e14 eV/m^3); limit scales as chi ~ 1/sqrt(rho_DM). CAVEATS: (1) This is a U(1)_B (baryon) coupling, NOT kinetic mixing (paper footnote 1 explicitly states so); reported on the DarkPhoton chi plane because the axis variable eps plays the role of chi. (2) For U(1)_{B-L} multiply eps^2 by 4 (i.e. chi by 2), per Fig. 3 caption. (3) Alternative convention: if the compilation stores the actual gauge coupling g = e*eps rather than chi=eps, multiply all y-values by e = 0.3028. These convention choices drive the moderate extraction_confidence.
